paths.description: Homepage: primary news discovery, consent, responsive and performance template.
Cronaca premium article: representative detail/paywall template.
Search results for “roma”: primary content-finding flow.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to dark color preference.
findings.evidence: With prefers-color-scheme: dark active, the body remains rgb(252,253,253) with black text and color-scheme remains normal; the dark screenshot is visually unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map surfaces/text to light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme theme.

findings.summary: High-contrast support and baseline contrast are insufficient.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors handling, and Lighthouse found 121 contrast failures on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast styles, preserve native control colors, and remediate all WCAG contrast failures.

findings.summary: Page and state changes use abrupt legacy swaps.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition usage across the representative news templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance section/article navigation and major state swaps with same- or cross-document View Transitions, honoring reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long news pages lack scroll-state guidance.
findings.evidence: The homepage is about 53,519 CSS px tall, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, scroll timeline, or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading/scroll progress affordance and progressively enhance sticky chrome with scroll-state-aware CSS.

findings.summary: The consent wall obscures the primary content on load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a large modal/overlay covering the news page before interaction; on mobile its controls extend below the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a compact, content-preserving consent surface, expose an equally prominent continue-without-accepting action, and defer nonessential tracking.

findings.summary: The blocking overlay is not built with a semantic dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The DOM reports zero dialog and zero popover elements while the screenshots show a modal consent experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for the modal flow with native focus containment/close semantics, or a nonmodal disclosure if blocking is unnecessary.

findings.summary: Advertising, subscription chrome, and consent UI dominate the first viewport.
findings.evidence: The article screenshot gives a large bordered ad slot most of the pre-headline viewport, and the consent layer occupies the lower portion.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce and defer ad chrome, reserve smaller stable slots, and prioritize headline/article content in the initial viewport.

findings.summary: The homepage forces a 986 px layout into a 390 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive measured scrollWidth 986 versus visual viewport 390, with 596 px horizontal overflow; the article template had no overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed desktop minimum widths and use intrinsic/fluid sizing so the homepage fits the visual viewport.

findings.summary: Reused news components do not use container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules, while the homepage fails at 390 px and the article template adapts correctly.
findings.suggestedFix: Make shared cards/header/ad modules size-contained and adapt them with container queries plus intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target support are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found many visible links/inputs with outline:none, and Lighthouse reported 10 target-size failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible with a high-contrast ring and ensure interactive targets meet minimum size/spacing without hover-only disclosure.

findings.summary: The primary news task is hidden behind consent and ad chrome.
findings.evidence: The homepage and section are identifiable, but the load screenshots cover the story grid with consent; the article places a large ad before the headline.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose the lead stories/headline immediately and move consent/ad choices out of the core content path.

findings.summary: Reading a public route is needlessly detoured through a coercive consent/subscription choice.
findings.evidence: On the homepage the CSS makes .iubenda-cs-close-btn visibility:hidden, leaving Accept or “Reject and subscribe”; the article uses another full-width cookie notice before reading.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer a visible continue-with-essential-cookies path on every template and keep subscription decisions separate from privacy consent.

findings.summary: Loading is far outside the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 11.8 s and article LCP 15.5 s; the trace independently measured homepage LCP 5.4 s. CLS remained low.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce document latency and blocking work, and defer noncritical ads/third parties.

findings.summary: Main-thread work remains heavy during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 3.0 s of main-thread work and 280 ms TBT; the trace found one 65 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up initialization, remove unused code, and defer analytics/ad work until needed.

findings.summary: Critical delivery has slow document and render-blocking paths.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 890 ms root-document latency, an estimated 1,340 ms render-blocking saving, and 710 KiB cache-lifetime saving; HAR confirmed two very-high-priority parser stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Improve HTML response latency, inline only critical CSS, defer remaining styles, and set effective immutable caching.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 729 KiB unused JavaScript and 13 KiB unused CSS; HAR transferred 1.51 MB across 30 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate/legacy bundles, code-split by template, and load third-party functionality only after user need/consent.

findings.summary: Some links and images lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and image-alt; the DOM probe counted 57 anchors with no text, aria-label, or image alt, and the image primitive found two missing alts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable link a discernible name and provide meaningful alt text or empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: Text contrast fails at scale.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified 121 homepage contrast failures and 3 article failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Update color tokens to meet WCAG AA in default and high-contrast modes, then retest all templates.

findings.summary: Heading structure and focus visibility are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The Politica section has no h1 and begins with repeated h2 headings; many focused visible links show outline:none in the probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive h1 per section, maintain logical heading levels, and add a persistent :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Homepage reflow and target sizing fail on mobile.
findings.evidence: At 390 px the homepage overflows by 596 px and Lighthouse reports 10 undersized/closely spaced targets; viewport scaling itself is allowed.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix intrinsic reflow, preserve pinch zoom, and enlarge/separate targets.

findings.summary: Document basics are sound, but image delivery has sizing defects.
findings.evidence: Doctype, UTF-8 and viewport are valid, but the image primitive found two missing dimensions on both homepage and article, 79/100 homepage images without srcset, and 94 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions/aspect-ratio and responsive modern image sources while retaining fallbacks.

findings.summary: DevTools reports an inspector issue.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found one Inspector Issues entry, although it found no deprecated APIs or console errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the reported inspector issue and keep source maps/library audits clean in CI.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable but some lack descriptive text and one section lacks an h1.
findings.evidence: The homepage has 581 real href anchors but 57 have no discernible text; Lighthouse fails link-name. Viewport and robots allow normal search crawling.
findings.suggestedFix: Name every link and preserve meaningful visible text in anchors; add the missing section h1.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protections are weak.
findings.evidence: CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; HSTS and nosniff are missing. Six of seven observed cookies lack Secure and all use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash CSP without unsafe-eval, add HSTS and nosniff, and mark cookies Secure with the narrowest SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The pre-consent third-party footprint is extensive.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 22 third-party origins and four known tracker domains; HAR transferred 2.16 MB, including 1.51 MB of scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Block nonessential third parties until explicit consent, consolidate analytics, batch events, and set a strict third-party budget.

findings.summary: Key browser-enforced defensive policies are absent or unsafe.
findings.evidence: Headers show no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking policy, or Permissions-Policy; Referrer-Policy is unsafe-url and CSP has no frame-ancestors while allowing unsafe code.
findings.suggestedFix: Set strict-origin-when-cross-origin, frame-ancestors, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, nosniff, and a hardened CSP/Trusted Types posture.

findings.summary: Runtime overlay behavior is inconsistent across templates and viewports.
findings.evidence: Homepage/section show a centered blocking wall, mobile places actions below the first viewport, and the article uses a different bottom notice; no semantic dialog is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Unify consent state in one resilient semantic component with focus management, viewport-safe sizing, and nonblocking fallback.

findings.summary: Language is declared, but layout CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: html lang is it, but CSS inspection found no logical properties and did find physical left/padding-left rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt logical inline/block properties and set direction deliberately where bidirectional content can occur.

findings.summary: Consent refusal is tied to purchasing a subscription.
findings.evidence: The primary choices are “ACCETTA” and “RIFIUTA E ABBONATI”; the homepage CSS hides the continue-without-accepting control, making the privacy-preserving path materially less available.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate privacy refusal from purchase, expose “continue with essential cookies” at equal prominence, and keep defaults unselected.

findings.summary: The commercial choice is entangled with consent refusal.
findings.evidence: The consent wall presents subscription as the rejection action, while pricing appears elsewhere; this makes a privacy choice look like a purchase commitment.
findings.suggestedFix: Decouple consent from subscription, show pricing/commitment before purchase, and offer clear cancellation and reauthentication within the account flow.

findings.summary: Image assets are not efficiently responsive.
findings.evidence: The homepage image audit found 94 legacy-format images, 79 without srcset, and eight oversized images; Lighthouse estimated 76 KiB immediate image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and width-based srcset/sizes, preserve dimensions, and match source resolution to display size.

findings.summary: Large script and third-party loads create avoidable work.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 83 requests and 2.16 MB transferred; 30 scripts account for 1.51 MB, while Lighthouse estimates 729 KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused bundles, defer offscreen/optional components, and prevent background analytics/ad work before consent.

findings.summary: Third-party code is disproportionate to the initial news task.
findings.evidence: Twenty-two third-party origins load on the homepage, including four known trackers, before the user can access content.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party request/byte budget, lazy-load user-value integrations, and keep trackers blocked until consent.

findings.summary: Repeated menu use retains substantial additional heap.
findings.evidence: After equivalent consent dismissal and settling, 10 menu open/close cycles increased snapshot self size from 75.1 MB to 81.9 MB (+9%) and snapshot nodes from 1.35M to 1.52M (+13%).
findings.suggestedFix: Profile allocation retainers across repeated menu cycles, remove listeners/closures on close, and bound third-party caches.

findings.summary: The homepage has an unusually large memory footprint for a news document.
findings.evidence: The settled baseline heap summary contains 1,348,055 snapshot nodes and 75.1 MB self size before repeated interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce DOM and script populations, virtualize/defer offscreen modules, and load advertising/analytics components conditionally.

findings.summary: Interaction-associated heap/node growth needs leak investigation.
findings.evidence: The settled repeated-interaction snapshot retained 176,820 more snapshot nodes and 6.8 MB more self size; the in-page sample also grew from 3,441 to 3,478 DOM elements. Constructor-level detached-node attribution was unavailable, so confidence is medium.
findings.suggestedFix: Use allocation instrumentation and listener/timer accounting around the menu lifecycle; release observers, timers, nodes and third-party references on close.

taskList.title: Fix homepage mobile overflow and accessible targets
Replace coercive blocking consent with a privacy-preserving semantic flow
Cut LCP, render-blocking resources, unused JavaScript and third-party work
Harden CSP, cookies and browser security headers
Repair contrast, names, heading structure and focus visibility
Investigate and bound menu/session memory growth
